--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

Throughout, G(v) := (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is the Gram matrix of v = (v₁,…,v_n) and, for a real n×n matrix B and τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n), (Bτ)_i := Σ_j B_ij τ_j. This is item (P1) of the parent proof.

1. (Second identity: change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector. By multilinearity,
 α(Bτ) = Σ_{g : Fin n → Fin n} (Π_i B_{i g(i)}) · α(τ_{g(1)}, …, τ_{g(n)}).
 If g is not injective two arguments coincide and the term vanishes because α is alternating. If g = σ is a permutation, α(τ∘σ) = sign(σ) α(τ). Hence α(Bτ) = (Σ_σ sign(σ) Π_i B_{iσ(i)}) α(τ) = det(B) α(τ) by the Leibniz formula (det B = det Bᵀ, so the row/column convention is immaterial). As this holds for every α, simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B) • simpleNVector τ. For n = 0 both sides are the functional α ↦ α(∅) and the determinant of the empty matrix is 1.

2. (Gram matrices transform by congruence.) G(Bτ)_{ik} = ⟨Σ_j B_ij τ_j, Σ_l B_kl τ_l⟩ = (B G(τ) Bᵀ)_{ik}; hence det G(Bτ) = det(B)² det G(τ).

3. (Upper bound for orthonormal families.) If τ is orthonormal then |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|τ_i| = ‖α‖ for every α, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ 1.

4. (Lower bound for orthonormal families.) Let τ be orthonormal (n ≥ 1), W := span τ and π_W the orthogonal projection onto W. Define α₀(u₁,…,u_n) := det(⟨u_i, τ_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear and alternating (a determinant whose i-th row depends linearly on u_i, and two equal u's give two equal rows) and continuous (finite dimension). The i-th row (⟨u_i,τ_j⟩)_j is the coordinate vector of π_W u_i in the orthonormal basis τ, of Euclidean length |π_W u_i| ≤ |u_i|. By Hadamard's inequality |det A| ≤ Π_i |row_i(A)| (proof: if the rows are dependent det A = 0; otherwise Gram–Schmidt on the rows gives A = R O with O orthogonal and R lower triangular with diagonal entries |a_i^⊥| ≤ |a_i|, a_i^⊥ the component of the i-th row orthogonal to the previous rows, so |det A| = Π|a_i^⊥| ≤ Π|a_i|; in Lean this is `Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le` for the volume form of W composed with π_W) we get |α₀(u)| ≤ Π|u_i|, i.e. ‖α₀‖ ≤ 1. Since α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩) = det I = 1, ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≥ |simpleNVector τ (α₀)| / ‖α₀‖ ≥ 1. Together with step 3: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 = det G(τ). For n = 0, 0-covectors are the constants c = α(∅) with ‖α‖ = |c|, so ‖simpleNVector ∅‖ = 1 = det of the empty matrix.

5. (Dependent families.) If v₁,…,v_n are linearly dependent then α(v) = 0 for every alternating α (`AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent`), so simpleNVector v = 0 and ‖simpleNVector v‖² = 0. Also G(v) is singular: for a nontrivial c with Σ_j c_j v_j = 0 we get G(v)c = (⟨v_i, Σ_j c_j v_j⟩)_i = 0, so det G(v) = 0. The first identity holds. (This covers in particular n > P.)

6. (Independent families.) If v is linearly independent, Gram–Schmidt produces an orthonormal τ with span τ = span v and v = Bτ, B_ij = ⟨v_i, τ_j⟩, B invertible. By step 1, simpleNVector v = det(B) • simpleNVector τ, so by step 4, ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B|. By step 2 and G(τ) = I, det G(v) = det(B)². Hence ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det G(v) = det (Matrix.of fun i j => ⟨v_i, v_j⟩).

Steps 5–6 give the first conjunct for every v; step 1 gives the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: Leibniz expansion and the alternating property give α(Bτ) = det(B)·α(τ) for every n-covector α, hence simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B)•simpleNVector τ.
Gram matrices transform by congruence: det G(Bτ) = det(B)²·det G(τ).
For orthonormal τ: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ Π|τ_i| = 1, and the covector det(⟨u_i,τ_j⟩) has norm ≤ 1 by Hadamard and value 1 at τ, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1.
Dependent families: simpleNVector v = 0 and det G(v) = 0.
Independent families: Gram–Schmidt v = Bτ gives ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B| and det G(v) = det(B)².

--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Source: Fact A in the parent proof's conventions (an alternating n-linear map is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, and dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}), proved here in full.

Notation:
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
- For a tuple v : Fin n → Fin P, e_v := (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}).
- I(n,P) := SimonMultiIndex n P = Fin n ↪o Fin P, a finite type.
- For β ∈ I(n,P), α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β and dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. (Kronecker property.) Let β, γ ∈ I(n,P). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^β(e_γ) = det M, where M_{ij} = proj(β(i))(e_{γ(j)}) is 1 if β(i) = γ(j) and 0 otherwise.
(a) If β = γ, then M_{ij} = 1 iff β(i) = β(j) iff i = j (β is injective). So M is the identity matrix and dx^β(e_β) = 1.
(b) If β ≠ γ, there is i with β(i) ∉ {γ(0),…,γ(n−1)}. Otherwise range β ⊆ range γ. Both ranges have exactly n elements because β and γ are injective (Set.ncard_range_of_injective), so range β = range γ (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le). An order embedding of the well-order Fin n is determined by its range (OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so β = γ, a contradiction. For this i, row i of M is zero, hence det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).
Thus dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}.
2. (Agreement on increasing tuples.) Let R := Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β, a continuous alternating n-linear map. For γ ∈ I(n,P), Step 1 gives R(e_γ) = Σ_β α(e_β)·δ_{βγ} = α(e_γ).
3. (Agreement on injective tuples.) Let v : Fin n → Fin P be injective, and let σ := Tuple.sort v, a permutation of Fin n with v∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). Since v∘σ is also injective, it is strictly increasing, so γ := v∘σ defines an element of I(n,P) (OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono) with e_γ = e_v∘σ. For every alternating map f, f(e_v∘σ) = sign(σ)·f(e_v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Applying this to α and to R and using Step 2 gives sign(σ)·α(e_v) = α(e_γ) = R(e_γ) = sign(σ)·R(e_v). Acting with sign(σ)⁻¹ (inv_smul_smul) yields α(e_v) = R(e_v).
4. (Conclusion.) Two alternating multilinear maps on ℝ^P that agree on all tuples (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}) with v injective are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis). Hence α and R are equal as alternating maps, and therefore as continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So α = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β.
5. (Degenerate cases.) Steps 1–4 cover them. For n = 0, I(0,P) has one element, dx^β is the constant covector 1, and the identity reads α = α(())·1. For n > P, I(n,P) is empty, so R = 0, and no injective v exists, so Step 4 gives α = 0 = R. ∎

Conventions. ℝ^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) (Lean `Eucl m`) with Euclidean norm |·| = ‖·‖; L(E, F) is the space of (continuous) linear maps with the operator norm; Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure (on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume); B_ρ(x) is the open ball. This is Steps 1 (pieces P_j), 2 (definition of L) and 3 (measurability) of the parent proof, carried out for an arbitrary countable family of charts. Hypotheses: for each j ∈ ℕ, Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ is open, Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is C¹, and there is c_j > 0 with c_j|w − w′| ≤ |Φ_j(w) − Φ_j(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω_j; f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q is an arbitrary map. Notation: S_j := Φ_j(Ω_j); A_j(w) := DΦ_j(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ_j w; B_j(w) := fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ_j) w (Mathlib's fderiv: the derivative where f∘Φ_j is differentiable at w and 0 otherwise); I := {A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^P) : A injective}.

0. (Left inverse.) By the sibling lemma lpf_tde_continuous_left_inverse (applied with n, P) there is Λ : L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^P) → L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ), continuous on I, with Λ(A)∘A = id_{ℝⁿ} and |AΛ(A)v| ≤ |v| for every A ∈ I and v ∈ ℝ^P.

1. (Φ_j is injective on Ω_j.) If w, w′ ∈ Ω_j and Φ_j(w) = Φ_j(w′), then c_j|w − w′| ≤ 0 with c_j > 0, so w = w′.

2. (S_j is Borel.) Ω_j is open, hence Borel; Φ_j is continuous (C¹) and injective on Ω_j (step 1); ℝⁿ is Polish. By the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn) S_j = Φ_j(Ω_j) is Borel. [Elementary alternative: Ω_j is the union of the countably many compact balls closedBall(q, r) ⊆ Ω_j with q ∈ ℚⁿ, r ∈ ℚ_{>0}; their images under the continuous Φ_j are compact, hence closed, so S_j is a countable union of closed sets.]

3. (Inverse chart.) Let Ψ_j : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ satisfy Ψ_j(x) ∈ Ω_j and Φ_j(Ψ_j(x)) = x for every x ∈ S_j (e.g. Ψ_j := Function.invFunOn Φ_j Ω_j; Mathlib invFunOn_mem, invFunOn_eq). For x, x′ ∈ S_j the antilipschitz bound gives c_j|Ψ_j(x) − Ψ_j(x′)| ≤ |Φ_j(Ψ_j(x)) − Φ_j(Ψ_j(x′))| = |x − x′|, so Ψ_j is (1/c_j)-Lipschitz, in particular continuous, on S_j.

4. (DΦ_j(w) is injective for w ∈ Ω_j.) Let w ∈ Ω_j, A := A_j(w) and s ∈ ℝⁿ. Φ_j is differentiable at w (C¹), so by the chain rule the curve γ(t) := Φ_j(w + ts) has derivative As at t = 0, i.e. the slopes (γ(t) − γ(0))/t tend to As as t → 0, t ≠ 0 (Mathlib hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope). Since Ω_j is open, w + ts ∈ Ω_j for all small |t|, and then |(γ(t) − γ(0))/t| = |Φ_j(w + ts) − Φ_j(w)|/|t| ≥ c_j|ts|/|t| = c_j|s| for t ≠ 0. Passing to the limit, |As| ≥ c_j|s|. Hence As = 0 implies s = 0, and by linearity A is injective: A_j(w) ∈ I.

5. (Borel measurability of each chart piece.) Define functions on ℝ^P (piecewise on the Borel set S_j):
   Ψ̃_j(x) := Ψ_j(x) if x ∈ S_j, 0 otherwise;
   Λ̃_j(x) := Λ(A_j(Ψ_j(x))) if x ∈ S_j, 0 otherwise;
   G_j(x) := B_j(Ψ̃_j(x)) ∘ Λ̃_j(x) if x ∈ S_j, 0 otherwise.
   (a) Ψ̃_j is Borel: it is continuous on the Borel set S_j (step 3) and constant on its complement (Mathlib ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise).
   (b) Λ̃_j is Borel: A_j = fderiv ℝ Φ_j is continuous since Φ_j is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv) and Ψ_j is continuous on S_j, so x ↦ A_j(Ψ_j(x)) is continuous on S_j; it maps S_j into I by step 4 (Ψ_j(x) ∈ Ω_j); Λ is continuous on I; hence x ↦ Λ(A_j(Ψ_j(x))) is continuous on S_j, and ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise applies again.
   (c) w ↦ B_j(w) = fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ_j) w is Borel measurable for every map f∘Φ_j, with no regularity assumption (Mathlib measurable_fderiv; L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^Q) carries its Borel σ-algebra), so x ↦ B_j(Ψ̃_j(x)) is Borel as a composition of Borel maps. Composition (T, S) ↦ T∘S : L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^Q) × L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ) → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) is continuous (bounded bilinear), and these finite-dimensional spaces are second countable, so x ↦ B_j(Ψ̃_j(x))∘Λ̃_j(x) is Borel (Mathlib Continuous.measurable2). Finally G_j is Borel as a piecewise combination of Borel maps on the Borel set S_j (Measurable.piecewise).

6. (Gluing by the first chart.) For x ∈ ℝ^P let p_j(x) be the statement "x ∈ S_j or x ∉ ⋃_i S_i". For every x some p_j(x) holds (if x ∈ ⋃_i S_i take j with x ∈ S_j, otherwise j = 0), and each set {x : p_j(x)} = S_j ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_i S_i) is Borel by step 2. Let j(x) be the least j with p_j(x) and define L(x) := G_{j(x)}(x). By the countable piecewise measurability lemma (Mathlib Measurable.find, with the Borel maps G_j and Borel sets {p_j}) L is Borel measurable. Since L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) is a finite-dimensional normed space (second countable and metrizable), L is strongly measurable (Measurable.stronglyMeasurable).

7. (L vanishes off the charts.) If x ∉ ⋃_i S_i, then in particular x ∉ S_{j(x)}, so L(x) = G_{j(x)}(x) = 0.

8. (Chart identities.) Let x ∈ ⋃_i S_i and j := j(x). Since "x ∉ ⋃_i S_i" is false, p_j(x) gives x ∈ S_j. Put w := Ψ_j(x); then w ∈ Ω_j and Φ_j(w) = x (step 3). Let A := A_j(w) ∈ I (step 4) and B := B_j(w). As x ∈ S_j, Ψ̃_j(x) = w and Λ̃_j(x) = Λ(A), so L(x) = G_j(x) = B∘Λ(A).
   (i) For s ∈ ℝⁿ: L(x)(As) = B(Λ(A)(As)) = B(s), because Λ(A)∘A = id (step 0). This is L x (fderiv ℝ (Φ j) w s) = fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ j) w s.
   (ii) For v ∈ ℝ^P put s := Λ(A)v. Then |As| = |AΛ(A)v| ≤ |v| (step 0) and L(x)v = B(Λ(A)v) = Bs.
   So j and w witness the last clause. Together with steps 6 and 7 this proves the statement. ∎ (n = 0 is included: then every linear map out of ℝ⁰ is 0 and all identities hold trivially.)

Φ_j is injective on Ω_j, S_j = Φ_j(Ω_j) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin or σ-compactness), and the inverse chart Ψ_j is (1/c_j)-Lipschitz on S_j.
For w ∈ Ω_j, |DΦ_j(w)s| ≥ c_j|s|, so DΦ_j(w) is injective.

L(x) := G_{first j with x ∈ S_j}(x), 0 off ⋃ S_j, is Borel by Measurable.find, hence strongly measurable.

Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and O ⊆ U open. For i = 1, 2 let (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M_i θ_i ξ_i. Suppose τ(M₁,θ₁,ξ₁)(ω) = τ(M₂,θ₂,ξ₂)(ω) for every ω ∈ Dᵏ(U) (TestFormOn U k) with tsupport ω ⊆ O, where τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) = tauAction k M θ ξ ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ. Then:
- Hᵏ((M₁ Δ M₂) ∩ O) = 0, and
- θ₁ = θ₂ and ξ₁ = ξ₂ hold Hᵏ⌞(M₁ ∩ O)-almost everywhere.

Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is item (P2) of the parent proof. Recall spt T = T.support = U ∖ Z_T, where Z_T (the zero region) is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, on which T vanishes (T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W).

1. Since M ⊆ U (field `subset`), M ∖ spt T ⊆ Z_T.

2. Z_T is an open subset of the second countable space ℝ^P, hence Lindelöf; so there are countably many sets W_k of the defining family with Z_T = ⋃_k W_k. By countable subadditivity it suffices to prove Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = 0 for every open W with K := closure W compact, K ⊆ U, on which T vanishes.

3. (ξ has unit norm a.e.) By the field `orients`, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. Hence ‖ξ(x)‖ = 1 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M; in particular ξ(x) ≠ 0 and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every n-covector α. 5. Fix an n-covector α and φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with tsupport φ ⊆ W. The form ω(x) := φ(x)α is smooth with compact support contained in W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and T(ω) = 0 because T vanishes on W. By the representation T = τ(M,θ,ξ):
 0 = T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(φ(x)α) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_M φ(x) θ(x) ξ(x)(α) dHⁿ(x) = ∫ φ g_α dν, with g_α(x) := ξ(x)(α),
 where we used that φ = 0 off W; all integrands are absolutely integrable since |φ θ ξ(α)| ≤ sup|φ| ‖α‖ θ 1_{M∩K} Hⁿ-a.e. on M by step 3.

6. g_α is ν-measurable (ξ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, field `aestronglyMeasurable`, and ν ≪ Hⁿ⌞M) and |g_α| ≤ ‖α‖ ν-a.e., so g_α is ν-integrable, hence locally ν-integrable on W. As ν is a finite (so locally finite) Borel measure and ∫ φ g_α dν = 0 for all φ ∈ C_c^∞ with tsupport in the open set W, the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations (Mathlib `IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero`; equivalently: the finite signed measure g_α ν⌞W annihilates C_c^∞(W), hence by uniform approximation of C_c(W) by mollification annihilates C_c(W), hence is the zero measure) gives g_α = 0 ν-a.e. on W.

7. Because θ > 0 on M, a subset of M ∩ W is ν-null iff it is Hⁿ-null. Hence ξ(x)(α) = 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ W. Let α₁,…,α_N be a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors on ℝ^P; intersecting the N full-measure sets, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ W the linear functional ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, so ξ(x) = 0.

8. Comparing with step 3 (ξ(x) ≠ 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M), we obtain Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = 0.

9. By steps 1, 2 and 8, Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) ≤ Σ_k Hⁿ(M ∩ W_k) = 0. ∎ (For n = 0 the same proof applies: 0-covectors are constants and ‖simpleNVector ∅‖ = 1.)

subproblems.title: Locality of weighted approximate tangent spaces
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, M, M′ ⊆ ℝ^P, θ, θ′ : ℝ^P → ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P and V ⊆ ℝ^P open with x ∈ V. Assume Hᵏ((M Δ M′) ∩ V) = 0 (Hᵏ = μHE[k]), θ = θ′ holds Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ V)-almost everywhere, and θ(x) = θ′(x). Then every linear subspace L ⊆ ℝ^P which is the weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L: dim L = k and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHᵏ(y) → θ(x)∫_L f dHᵏ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x)) is also the weighted approximate tangent space of (M′, θ′) at x.

The parent applies it with V = ℝ^P at H^k-a.e. x ∈ M (where θ(x) = θ′(x)), using H^k(M Δ M′) = 0 and θ = θ′ H^k⌞M-a.e. from the sibling tau_unique: every weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x is one of (M′, θ′). This transfers the derivative property of the premise's L′ from (M′, θ′) to (M, θ), which is the hypothesis on L of the sibling chart_convergence (it replaces (II.7b–c)).

--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Source: the locality step (P5)(iv)/(P3) of the parent proof (“the weighted approximate tangent space at x only depends on M, θ near x, modulo Hᵏ-null sets; for small r the blow-up integrals only see x + r·spt f ⊆ V, and Hᵏ(η_{x,r}Z) = r^{−k}Hᵏ(Z) = 0 for null Z”), written out against the frozen definition `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt` (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7). This argument has been kernel-checked against the frozen definitions (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only).

Notation. H := Hᵏ = `μHE[k]` on ℝ^P. For r > 0, η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (`blowUpMap x r`). By definition, `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L` means: dim L = k (`finrank ℝ L = k`), and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ), I_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) → θ(x)∫_L f dH as r ↓ 0 (limit along 𝓝[>]0).

1. (Null sets under blow-up.) If r > 0 and H(Z) = 0 then H(η_r(Z)) = 0. Indeed |η_r(a) − η_r(b)| = r⁻¹|a − b|, so η_r is Lipschitz with constant r⁻¹ and μH[k](η_r(Z)) ≤ r^{−k}μH[k](Z) (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le`). Moreover H = c_k·μH[k] with c_k ∈ (0,∞) (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`, `addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`), so H(Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](η_r(Z)) = 0 ⇒ H(η_r(Z)) = 0.
2. (Elementary facts on η_r.) For r > 0, η_r is a bijection of ℝ^P with inverse y ↦ x + ry. Hence η_r(A ∩ B) = η_r(A) ∩ η_r(B), η_r(A ∖ B) = η_r(A) ∖ η_r(B) for all A, B, and η_r(V) = {y : x + ry ∈ V} is open (preimage of the open V under a continuous map).
3. (Reduction.) The dimension conditions for (M,θ) and (M′,θ′) are the same condition on L. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ). Choose R > 0 with f(y) = 0 whenever |y| ≥ R (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded), and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ V (V open, x ∈ V). We prove I_{M,θ}(r) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) for every r ∈ (0, δ/R). Since (0, δ/R) ∈ 𝓝[>]0, the two functions of r agree eventually as r ↓ 0, so I_{M′,θ′}(r) has the same limit θ(x)∫_L f dH, which equals θ′(x)∫_L f dH because θ(x) = θ′(x). This gives `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M′ θ′ x L`.
4. (Integrands vanish off η_r(V).) Let r ∈ (0, δ/R), g : ℝ^P → ℝ arbitrary, F_g(y) := f(y)g(x + ry). If y ∉ η_r(V) then x + ry ∉ V ⊇ B_δ(x), so r|y| ≥ δ, hence |y| ≥ δ/r > R, f(y) = 0 and F_g(y) = 0.
5. (Step A: cutting by V.) For every S ⊆ ℝ^P and every g: ∫_{η_r(S)} F_g dH = ∫_{η_r(S∩V)} F_g dH. Indeed η_r(S ∩ V) = η_r(S) ∩ η_r(V) (step 2); since η_r(V) is open (measurable), H⌞(η_r(V) ∩ η_r(S)) = (H⌞η_r(S))⌞η_r(V) (`Measure.restrict_restrict`); and the integral of F_g with respect to (H⌞η_r(S))⌞η_r(V) equals its integral with respect to H⌞η_r(S), because F_g vanishes off η_r(V) (step 4; `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero`).
6. (Step C: replacing θ by θ′.) ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_θ dH = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_{θ′} dH. By hypothesis (H⌞(M∩V)){z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} = 0, so there is a Borel set N ⊇ {z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} with (H⌞(M∩V))(N) = H(N ∩ (M∩V)) = 0 (`exists_measurable_superset_of_null`, `Measure.restrict_apply`). Let N′ := {y : x + ry ∈ N}, a Borel set. Then {y : F_θ(y) ≠ F_{θ′}(y)} ⊆ N′, and N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V) ⊆ η_r(N ∩ (M∩V)) (if y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M ∩ V and x + ry = z ∈ N). By step 1 the right side is H-null, so (H⌞η_r(M∩V))(N′) = H(N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V)) = 0; thus F_θ = F_{θ′} (H⌞η_r(M∩V))-a.e. and the integrals agree (`integral_congr_ae`).
7. (Step B: replacing M by M′.) η_r(M∩V) and η_r(M′∩V) are H-a.e. equal sets: by step 2 their differences are η_r((M∩V)∖(M′∩V)) and η_r((M′∩V)∖(M∩V)), both contained in η_r((M Δ M′) ∩ V), which is H-null by the hypothesis H((M Δ M′) ∩ V) = 0 and step 1. Hence H⌞η_r(M∩V) = H⌞η_r(M′∩V) (`ae_eq_set`, `Measure.restrict_congr_set`).
8. (Conclusion.) For r ∈ (0, δ/R): I_{M,θ}(r) = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)}F_θ dH (step 5) = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)}F_{θ′} dH (step 6) = ∫_{η_r(M′∩V)}F_{θ′} dH (step 7) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) (step 5 applied to M′, θ′). By step 3 the lemma is proved. No measurability of M, M′, θ, θ′ is used.
proof_key_steps: Blow-up maps η_r(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) are Lipschitz, so they map Hᵏ-null sets to Hᵏ-null sets.
Choose R with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and δ with B_δ(x) ⊆ V; for r < δ/R the blow-up integrands vanish off the open set η_r(V).
Hence each blow-up integral over η_r(S) equals the one over η_r(S ∩ V).
On η_r(M ∩ V) the weights θ(x+r·) and θ′(x+r·) agree a.e., and η_r(M∩V), η_r(M′∩V) are a.e. equal.
The blow-up integrals of (M,θ) and (M′,θ′) coincide for all small r and θ(x) = θ′(x), so the limits and hence the weighted tangent spaces agree.

Fonseca, G. Leoni, J. Malý, Weak continuity and lower semicontinuity results for determinants, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 178 (2005) 411–448, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00205-005-0377-2; L. C. Evans, Partial Differential Equations, §8.1.4(b), Lemma 1 for the divergence-free rows of cofactor matrices).

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k with Lebesgue measure dw = volume; e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 (b ∈ Fin k). For a map v : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q, v^a := EuclideanSpace.proj a ∘ v (a ∈ Fin Q), ∂_bv(w) := Dv(w)e_b = fderiv ℝ v w e_b (Mathlib's fderiv, which is 0 where v is not differentiable) and ∂_bv^a(w) := (∂_bv(w))^a. For r ∈ ℕ, a : Fin r → Fin Q and b : Fin r → Fin k let M_{a,b}(v)(w) := det(∂_{b(s)}v^{a(t)}(w))_{t,s ∈ Fin r} (an r×r minor of the Jacobian matrix; the empty determinant is 1). Covectors carry the operator norm (|β(v₁,…,v_k)| ≤ ‖β‖Π|v_s|) and ‖α‖_∞ := sup_y‖α(y)‖ < ∞ (α is continuous with compact support). I(k,Q) := SimonMultiIndex k Q, dy^γ := wedgeCovectors k (fun t => EuclideanSpace.proj (γ t)), α_γ(y) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate (α y) γ = α(y)(e_{γ(0)},…,e_{γ(k−1)}).

0. (Rademacher bounds; integrability.) Let v be C-Lipschitz on Ω. By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem; Ω is open, so differentiability within Ω at w ∈ Ω is differentiability at w), v is differentiable at a.e. w ∈ Ω; at such w, v is C-Lipschitz on a ball around w, so ‖Dv(w)‖ ≤ C; at the other points Dv(w) = 0. Hence |∂_bv^a(w)| ≤ C for all w ∈ Ω, and by the Leibniz formula |M_{a,b}(v)(w)| ≤ r!·C^r on Ω. The map w ↦ Dv(w) is Borel (Mathlib measurable_fderiv) and v is continuous on Ω, so w ↦ α(v(w))(∂_0v(w),…,∂_{k−1}v(w)) is a.e.-strongly measurable on Ω and bounded by ‖α‖_∞C^k there. Multiplied by ψ it is integrable on Ω. All integrals below exist (for u_j, j ∈ ℕ, and for u₀).

1. (Reduction to minors.) By the sibling covector_expansion, α(y) = Σ_{γ∈I(k,Q)} α_γ(y)•dy^γ for every y, and by SimonGMT wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dy^γ(v_0,…,v_{k−1}) = det(EuclideanSpace.proj (γ t) (v_s))_{t,s} = det((v_s)^{γ(t)})_{t,s}. Taking v_s := ∂_sv(w): α(v(w))(∂_0v(w),…,∂_{k−1}v(w)) = Σ_γ α_γ(v(w))·M_{γ,id}(v)(w), where id : Fin k → Fin k is the identity. The sum over γ is finite, so it suffices to show for each γ ∈ I(k,Q):
 ∫_Ω ψ·(α_γ∘u_j)·M_{γ,id}(u_j) dw → ∫_Ω ψ·(α_γ∘u₀)·M_{γ,id}(u₀) dw.

2. (Splitting.) The difference of the two sides equals D₁(j) + D₂(j) with D₁(j) := ∫_Ω ψ(α_γ∘u_j − α_γ∘u₀)M_{γ,id}(u_j) and D₂(j) := ∫_Ω ψ(α_γ∘u₀)(M_{γ,id}(u_j) − M_{γ,id}(u₀)).
 (a) α_γ is continuous with compact support, hence bounded and uniformly continuous; since sup_{w∈Ω}|u_j(w) − u₀(w)| → 0 (uniform convergence on Ω), ε_j := sup_{w∈Ω}|α_γ(u_j(w)) − α_γ(u₀(w))| → 0, and by Step 0 |D₁(j)| ≤ ε_j·k!C^k·∫_Ω|ψ| → 0.
 (b) η := ψ·(α_γ∘u₀) is integrable on Ω (α_γ is bounded and α_γ∘u₀ is continuous on Ω). By the Claim of Step 3 with v_j := u_j, v := u₀, r := k, a := γ, b := id, we get D₂(j) → 0.

3. (Claim: weak-* convergence of minors.) Let v_j (j ∈ ℕ) and v be maps ℝ^k → ℝ^Q, all C-Lipschitz on Ω, with v_j → v uniformly on Ω. Then for all r ∈ ℕ, a : Fin r → Fin Q, b : Fin r → Fin k and every η integrable on Ω: ∫_Ω η·M_{a,b}(v_j) → ∫_Ω η·M_{a,b}(v). Proof by induction on r (for all a, b, η simultaneously).
 (3.0) (Smooth test functions suffice.) Assume the convergence for all φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω) (C^∞, compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ Ω). Given η integrable on Ω and ε > 0, choose φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω) with ∫_Ω|η − φ| < ε (C_c^∞(Ω) is dense in L¹(Ω): approximate η·1_Ω in L¹ by a continuous function with compact support in the open set Ω and mollify it). By Step 0, |∫ηM_{a,b}(v_j) − ∫ηM_{a,b}(v)| ≤ 2·r!C^r·ε + |∫φ(M_{a,b}(v_j) − M_{a,b}(v))|, and the claim for η follows. Fix φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω) and K := tsupport φ (compact, K ⊆ Ω).
 (3.1) (r = 0.) M_{a,b} ≡ 1 and there is nothing to prove.
 (3.2) (Integration-by-parts identity.) Let r ≥ 1. For q ∈ Fin r let a′ : Fin (r−1) → Fin Q list a(1),…,a(r−1) (all rows except row 0), b^{(q)} : Fin (r−1) → Fin k list b without its q-th entry, and C_q(v) := (−1)^q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v), the cofactor of the entry (0,q). Laplace expansion along row 0 gives M_{a,b}(v) = Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}v^{a(0)}·C_q(v). We prove, for every map v that is C-Lipschitz on Ω,
 (P) ∫_Ω φ·M_{a,b}(v) dw = −Σ_q ∫_Ω v^{a(0)}·C_q(v)·∂_{b(q)}φ dw.
 (i) Piola identity. If v is C² on a neighbourhood of K, then Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}[C_q(v)] = 0 there. For r = 1, C_0 ≡ 1. For r ≥ 2 let R_t := (∂_{b(0)}v^{a(t)},…,∂_{b(r−1)}v^{a(t)}) (t = 1,…,r−1) and let ε_q be the q-th unit row vector; expanding along row 0, C_q(v) = det N_q where N_q has row 0 equal to ε_q and row t equal to R_t. Differentiating the determinant row by row, ∂_{b(q)}det N_q = Σ_{t≥1} det(N_q with row t replaced by ∂_{b(q)}R_t), and ∂_{b(q)}R_t = Σ_s H^t_{qs}ε_s with H^t_{qs} := ∂_{b(q)}∂_{b(s)}v^{a(t)}. Hence Σ_q∂_{b(q)}C_q(v) = Σ_{t≥1}Σ_{q,s}H^t_{qs}·D_t(q,s), where D_t(q,s) is the determinant of the matrix with row 0 equal to ε_q, row t equal to ε_s and the remaining rows R_u. H^t is symmetric in (q,s) (Schwarz's theorem, v ∈ C²) and D_t is antisymmetric in (q,s) (exchange of rows 0 and t), so every double sum vanishes.
 (ii) (P) for v of class C² near K. By (i), M_{a,b}(v) = Σ_q[∂_{b(q)}v^{a(0)}·C_q(v) + v^{a(0)}·∂_{b(q)}C_q(v)] = Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}(v^{a(0)}C_q(v)) near K. Multiplying by φ and integrating by parts in the direction e_{b(q)} (φ is C^∞ with compact support K ⊆ Ω, v^{a(0)}C_q(v) is C¹ near K) gives (P).
 (iii) (P) for v C-Lipschitz on Ω. Choose d > 0 with K_{3d} := {w : dist(w,K) ≤ 3d} ⊆ Ω (K compact, Ω open). Extend each coordinate v^a|_Ω to a C-Lipschitz function ṽ^a on ℝ^k (McShane extension, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real); then ṽ = v on Ω, so Dṽ = Dv at every point of Ω where either is differentiable, and |∂_bṽ^a| ≤ C everywhere. Let ρ_δ (0 < δ < d) be a standard mollifier (C^∞, ≥ 0, supported in the ball B_δ(0), ∫ρ_δ = 1) and v_δ := ρ_δ * ṽ componentwise. Then v_δ is C^∞; v_δ → ṽ uniformly on ℝ^k as δ → 0 (ṽ is uniformly continuous); ∂_bv_δ = ρ_δ * ∂_bṽ (differentiate under the integral sign: the difference quotients (ṽ(z + te_b) − ṽ(z))/t are bounded by C and converge a.e. to ∂_bṽ(z) by Rademacher, so dominated convergence applies), hence |∂_bv_δ^a| ≤ C; and ∂_bv_δ → ∂_bṽ a.e. along any sequence δ_m → 0 (Lebesgue differentiation for mollifiers, Mathlib ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable). Apply (ii) to v_{δ_m} and let m → ∞: on K the integrands φ·M_{a,b}(v_{δ_m}) and v_{δ_m}^{a(0)}C_q(v_{δ_m})∂_{b(q)}φ converge a.e. (M_{a,b} and C_q are polynomials in the first derivatives) and are bounded by r!C^r|φ| and (sup_K|ṽ| + 1)(r−1)!C^{r−1}|∂_{b(q)}φ| respectively (for large m), which are integrable and vanish off K; dominated convergence gives (P) for ṽ. Since ṽ = v on Ω and Dṽ = Dv a.e. on K ⊆ Ω, (P) holds for v.
 (3.3) (Induction step, r ≥ 1.) By (P) for v_j and for v,
 ∫φM_{a,b}(v_j) − ∫φM_{a,b}(v) = −Σ_q[∫(v_j^{a(0)} − v^{a(0)})C_q(v_j)∂_{b(q)}φ + ∫v^{a(0)}(C_q(v_j) − C_q(v))∂_{b(q)}φ].
 The first integral is bounded by sup_Ω|v_j − v|·(r−1)!C^{r−1}·∫|∂_{b(q)}φ| → 0 (Step 0 for the cofactors). The second tends to 0 by the induction hypothesis for the (r−1)×(r−1) minors C_q = ±M_{a′,b^{(q)}}, tested against η_q := v^{a(0)}∂_{b(q)}φ, which is integrable on Ω (bounded, since v is continuous on the compact K, and supported in K). Hence ∫φM_{a,b}(v_j) → ∫φM_{a,b}(v); with (3.0) the Claim is proved.

4. (Conclusion.) Steps 2(a), 2(b) and 3 give D₁(j) + D₂(j) → 0 for every γ ∈ I(k,Q); summing over the finitely many γ (Step 1) proves the statement. Degenerate cases: for k = 0 the integrand is ψ(w)α(u_j(w))(()), I(0,Q) has a single element with M ≡ 1, and Step 2(a) alone suffices; for Q < k, Covector (Eucl Q) k = 0 (I(k,Q) is empty in the expansion), so both sides are 0; Ω = ∅ is trivial. ∎
proof_key_steps: Rademacher: |∂_bu^a| ≤ C on Ω, so all integrands are dominated by ‖α‖_∞C^k|ψ| and every minor of order r is bounded by r!C^r.
Sibling covector_expansion and wedgeCovectors_apply_det: α(u)(∂_0u,…,∂_{k−1}u) = Σ_γ α_γ(u)·M_γ(Du), a finite sum of k×k Jacobian minors.
Splitting: uniform continuity of α_γ and uniform convergence handle ψ(α_γ∘u_j − α_γ∘u₀)M_γ(Du_j); the rest is weak-* convergence of minors tested against ψ·(α_γ∘u₀) ∈ L¹(Ω).

Weak-* convergence of minors by induction on the order: density of C_c^∞(Ω) in L¹(Ω), and ∫φM = −Σ_q∫v^{a(0)}C_q∂_{b(q)}φ from Laplace expansion and the Piola identity (symmetric Hessian against antisymmetric determinants), extended from C² to Lipschitz maps by mollification.
Induction step: uniform convergence of v_j and the induction hypothesis for the cofactors tested against v^{a(0)}∂_{b(q)}φ.

subproblems.title: Measurability of the tangential push-forward k-vector field for an arbitrary admissible L (measurability claim of parent step (c))
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, H^k := μHE[k] on ℝ^P, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be locally Lipschitz on U and let L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) be any map (no measurability is assumed) such that for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, for every linear subspace T_x that is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x T_x) and every v ∈ T_x, the map t ↦ f(x + t v) has derivative L(x)v at t = 0. Then the k-vector field x ↦ L(x)_#ξ(x) = nVectorPushforward k (L x) (ξ x) is H^k⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q k : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q)), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Tx : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x Tx → ∀ v ∈ Tx, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => f (x + t • v)) (L x v) 0) → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => nVectorPushforward k (L x) (ξ x)) ((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the measurability assertion of step (c) of the parent proof (“F is H^k⌞M-measurable: on each chart piece G_i of (e), F∘Φ_i is given by the formula of (f) … in terms of θ∘Φ_i, the measurable coefficient c and the minors of Du (Du is Borel, as an a.e. limit of difference quotients), and Φ_i⁻¹ maps H^k-null sets to L^k-null sets”), proved for the k-vector field x ↦ L(x)_#ξ(x) itself — the parent's F is θ(x) times its value at ω(g(x)) — for an arbitrary open U, locally Lipschitz f and arbitrary L with the derivative property. As in the parent the argument is chart by chart. Its chart ingredients are the siblings c1_cover (the C¹ charts of step (e)), chart_chain_rule (the tangent identification and chain rule of step (f)) and measurable_chart_differential (a Borel map reproducing the chart derivatives D(f∘Φ_j) through continuous left inverses of DΦ_j; this is the parent's “Du is Borel” plus the inverse chart).

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P and L^k := volume on ℝ^k, which equals μHE[k] on ℝ^k (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume with finrank ℝ^k = k). DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w. For a linear A : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, A_# := nVectorPushforward k A = (w ↦ w ∘ covectorPullback k A); it satisfies A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A∘v) (SimonGMT nVectorPushforward_simple) and A_#(−w) = −A_#w. A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. Put V(x) := L(x)_#ξ(x).

1. (Charts.) M is countably k-rectifiable (field countablyRectifiable of the triple). By the sibling c1_cover there are C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝ^k → ℝ^P and open sets Ω_j ⊆ ℝ^k (j ∈ ℕ) such that Φ_j is K_j-Lipschitz and c_j-antilipschitz on Ω_j for some K_j ≥ 0, c_j > 0, and H(M ∖ ⋃_jΦ_j(Ω_j)) = 0.

2. (A Borel comparison map.) By the sibling measurable_chart_differential, applied to the family (Φ_j, Ω_j)_j of step 1 and to f, there is a strongly measurable L̂ : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) such that every x ∈ ⋃_jΦ_j(Ω_j) admits j ∈ ℕ and w ∈ Ω_j with Φ_j(w) = x and L̂(x)(DΦ_j(w)s) = D(f∘Φ_j)(w)s for every s ∈ ℝ^k.

3. (Good parameters.) Fix j and put S_j := Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(M). By the sibling chart_chain_rule (hypotheses: U open, the triple, f locally Lipschitz on U, the derivative hypothesis on L, Ω_j open, Φ_j C¹ and antilipschitz on Ω_j), for L^k-a.e. w ∈ S_j: (i) range DΦ_j(w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at Φ_j(w), and (ii) f∘Φ_j has Fréchet derivative L(Φ_j(w))∘DΦ_j(w) at w, hence D(f∘Φ_j)(w) = L(Φ_j(w))∘DΦ_j(w). Let B_j be the set of w ∈ ℝ^k at which (i) or (ii) fails, so (L^k⌞S_j)(B_j) = 0; let T_j be a measurable hull of B_j for L^k⌞S_j (Mathlib toMeasurable) and E_j := T_j ∩ S_j. Then E_j ⊆ Ω_j, L^k(E_j) = (L^k⌞S_j)(T_j) = (L^k⌞S_j)(B_j) = 0, and (i), (ii) hold at every w ∈ S_j ∖ E_j.

4. (An H-null exceptional set.) Φ_j is K_j-Lipschitz on E_j ⊆ Ω_j, so H(Φ_j(E_j)) ≤ K_j^k·μHE[k](E_j) = K_j^k·L^k(E_j) = 0 (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). Let Z_or be the set of x ∈ M at which the orientation clause of the triple fails; it is H-null (field orients, M null-measurable). Hence N := (M ∖ ⋃_jΦ_j(Ω_j)) ∪ ⋃_jΦ_j(E_j) ∪ Z_or is H-null (countable subadditivity and step 1).

5. (Pointwise identity off N.) Let x ∈ M ∖ N. By the orientation clause, ξ(x) = ε·simpleNVector τ with ε ∈ {1, −1}, τ : Fin k → ℝ^P orthonormal and span τ a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x. Since x ∈ ⋃_jΦ_j(Ω_j), step 2 provides j and w ∈ Ω_j with Φ_j(w) = x and L̂(x)∘DΦ_j(w) = D(f∘Φ_j)(w). Then w ∈ S_j (as Φ_j(w) = x ∈ M) and w ∉ E_j (otherwise x ∈ Φ_j(E_j) ⊆ N), so (i) and (ii) of step 3 hold at w. By (i), range DΦ_j(w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x; as θ(x) > 0 (field pos), weighted approximate tangent spaces at x are unique (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so span τ = range DΦ_j(w). Hence each τ_a equals DΦ_j(w)s_a for some s_a ∈ ℝ^k, and by step 2 and (ii), L̂(x)τ_a = D(f∘Φ_j)(w)s_a = L(x)(DΦ_j(w)s_a) = L(x)τ_a. Therefore L̂(x)∘τ = L(x)∘τ and
 V(x) = L(x)_#(ε·simpleNVector τ) = ε·simpleNVector(L(x)∘τ) = ε·simpleNVector(L̂(x)∘τ) = L̂(x)_#ξ(x).

6. (Conclusion.) The map (A, w) ↦ A_#w = w ∘ covectorPullback k A from L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) × NVector(ℝ^P, k) to NVector(ℝ^Q, k) is continuous: A ↦ covectorPullback k A is continuous (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM) and composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous. L̂ is strongly measurable and ξ is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable), so x ↦ L̂(x)_#ξ(x) is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. By step 5 it agrees with V at every point of M ∖ N, i.e. H⌞M-a.e. (M is null-measurable and H(N) = 0). Hence V is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. No case distinction is needed: for k = 0 (empty families; span of the empty family is {0}) and for k > P (then H = 0 on ℝ^P) the same argument applies verbatim. ∎

Key library names: toMeasurable, Measure.restrict_apply, measure_iUnion_null, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume (V := Eucl k) with finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, ae_restrict_iff'₀, measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, HasFDerivAt.fderiv, nVectorPushforward_simple, ContinuousLinearMap.neg_comp, AEStronglyMeasurable.congr.
proof_key_steps: Sibling c1_cover: C¹ charts Φ_j, Lipschitz and antilipschitz on open Ω_j, cover M up to an H^k-null set.
Sibling measurable_chart_differential: a strongly measurable L̂ with L̂(x)∘DΦ_j(w) = D(f∘Φ_j)(w) at a chart preimage w of every covered point x.
Sibling chart_chain_rule: outside an L^k-null E_j ⊆ Ω_j, range DΦ_j(w) is a weighted tangent space at Φ_j(w) and D(f∘Φ_j)(w) = L(Φ_j(w))∘DΦ_j(w); Φ_j(E_j) is H^k-null by the Lipschitz image bound.
Off an H^k-null set: ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ, uniqueness of weighted tangent spaces gives span τ = range DΦ_j(w), hence L̂(x)τ_a = L(x)τ_a and L(x)_#ξ(x) = L̂(x)_#ξ(x).
(A, w) ↦ A_#w is continuous, so x ↦ L̂(x)_#ξ(x) is H^k⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, and therefore so is x ↦ L(x)_#ξ(x).

subproblems.title: C¹ push-forward integrals converge to the tangential push-forward (part (I) of the consistency step)
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, H^k := μHE[k] on ℝ^P, and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple univ k M θ ξ. Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be Λ-Lipschitz and L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) such that for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, for every linear subspace T_x that is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x T_x) and every v ∈ T_x, the map t ↦ g(x + t v) has derivative L(x)v at t = 0. Assume θ is H^k-integrable on M ∩ g⁻¹(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^Q. Let g_j : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q (j ∈ ℕ) be C¹ maps, Λ′-Lipschitz for one common Λ′, converging uniformly to g on ℝ^P, and let ω : ℝ^Q → Covector (Eucl Q) k be continuous with compact support. Then ∫_M θ(x)·(Dg_j(x)_#ξ(x))(ω(g_j(x))) dH^k(x) → ∫_M θ(x)·(L(x)_#ξ(x))(ω(g(x))) dH^k(x) as j → ∞, where A_# = nVectorPushforward k A and Dg_j(x) = fderiv ℝ (g_j) x.

Source: part (I) of the parent proof (steps (a)–(g)), with these specializations, each of which only removes data that (I) does not use: (1) the tangential differential L(x) = d^Mg_x∘π_{T_xM} of the parent is replaced by an arbitrary map L having the directional-derivative property on the weighted approximate tangent spaces of (M,θ) — this property is the only one of d^Mg used in (c) and (f) (in the parent assembly L is the map L′ of IsLipschitzPushforward, transferred to (M,θ) by tangent locality; the parent's (II.7b–c) shows that L′ and d^Mg agree on T_xM); (2) the compactness of g⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X and H^k(M ∖ spt X) = 0 of step (b) are replaced by their only consequence used, the integrability of θ on M ∩ g⁻¹(K) for compact K; (3) the test form is only required to be continuous with compact support; (4) the ingredients of (c), (e) and (f) are the siblings: c1_cover (the chart cover of (e)), chart_chain_rule (tangent identification and chain rule of (f)), chart_change_of_variables (the area formula for the injective chart in (f)), simple_nvector_algebra (unit and change-of-frame facts), pushforward_measurable (the measurability of F claimed in (c)) and minor_weak_continuity (the weak continuity of minors and the final estimate of (f)).

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P; on ℝ^k, μHE[k] = L^k = volume. For a linear A : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, A_# := nVectorPushforward k A, (A_#w)(β) = w(covectorPullback k A β) with covectorPullback k A β = β(A·,…,A·); A_# is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A∘v) (SimonGMT nVectorPushforward_simple); simpleNVector v (β) = β(v). Covectors and k-vectors carry operator norms, |β(v_0,…,v_{k−1})| ≤ ‖β‖·Π|v_b|, and ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_y‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). F_j(x) := θ(x)·(Dg_j(x)_#ξ(x))(ω(g_j(x))) with Dg_j(x) := fderiv ℝ (gj j) x, and F(x) := θ(x)·(L(x)_#ξ(x))(ω(g(x))), are the integrands of the statement. e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1, ∂_bφ(w) := fderiv ℝ φ w e_b, ∂φ(w) := (∂_0φ(w),…,∂_{k−1}φ(w)), and JΦ(w) := (det(⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩)_{a,b})^{1/2}. A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

0. (Degenerate dimension.) If k > P then H = 0 on ℝ^P (μHE[k] is a constant multiple of μH[k], and μH[k](ℝ^P) = 0 because k exceeds the Hausdorff dimension P of ℝ^P), so both sides are 0. The argument below is valid for every k; for k = 0 all families are empty, simpleNVector of the empty family has norm 1, and JΦ ≡ 1.

1. (A fixed compact target set; parent (a).) Let K₀ := tsupport ω (compact) and K := {y : dist(y, K₀) ≤ 1} (compact; empty if K₀ = ∅). By uniform convergence choose j₀ with |g_j(x) − g(x)| < 1 for all x ∈ ℝ^P and all j ≥ j₀. For such j: if ω(g_j(x)) ≠ 0 then g_j(x) ∈ K₀, so g(x) ∈ K; and if ω(g(x)) ≠ 0 then g(x) ∈ K₀ ⊆ K. Hence F_j(x) = 0 and F(x) = 0 whenever g(x) ∉ K (j ≥ j₀). Only the tail j ≥ j₀ matters for the limit.

2. (One dominator; parent (c).) For H⌞M-a.e. x: (i) by the orientation clause of the triple, ξ(x) = ε·simpleNVector τ with ε ∈ {1, −1}, τ orthonormal and span τ a weighted approximate tangent space of (M,θ) at x; (ii) by the hypothesis on L, for each a the map t ↦ g(x + tτ_a) has derivative L(x)τ_a at t = 0, so |L(x)τ_a| ≤ Λ (g is Λ-Lipschitz and |τ_a| = 1). At such x, (A_#ξ(x))(β) = ε·β(Aτ_0,…,Aτ_{k−1}) for every linear A and covector β. Since g_j is differentiable and Λ′-Lipschitz, ‖Dg_j(x)‖ ≤ Λ′. With step 1, for j ≥ j₀: |F_j(x)| ≤ G(x) and |F(x)| ≤ G(x), where G := ‖ω‖_∞·Λ″^k·θ·1_{g⁻¹(K)} and Λ″ := max(Λ, Λ′). G is H⌞M-integrable, because θ is H-integrable on M ∩ g⁻¹(K) by hypothesis.

3. (Measurability and integrability.) θ is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable: it is H-integrable on M ∩ B̄_q(0) for each q ∈ ℕ (field integrableOn of the triple with U = ℝ^P), and M = ⋃_q(M ∩ B̄_q(0)). F_j: the covector field x ↦ covectorPullback k (Dg_j(x)) (ω(g_j(x))) is continuous (g_j is C¹, so Dg_j is continuous; A ↦ covectorPullback k A is continuous, Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM; ω∘g_j is continuous), ξ is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and the evaluation (w, β) ↦ w(β) is continuous; so F_j(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(covectorPullback k (Dg_j(x)) (ω(g_j(x)))) is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. F: by the sibling pushforward_measurable (with U := ℝ^P, which is open, the given triple, f := g, which is locally Lipschitz on ℝ^P because it is Lipschitz, and the hypothesis on L), x ↦ L(x)_#ξ(x) is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, and ω∘g is continuous; so F is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. Together with step 2, F_j (j ≥ j₀) and F are H⌞M-integrable.

4. (Chart pieces; parent (e).) M is countably k-rectifiable, so the sibling c1_cover gives C¹ maps Φ_i : ℝ^k → ℝ^P and open Ω_i ⊆ ℝ^k (i ∈ ℕ), Φ_i K_i-Lipschitz and c_i-antilipschitz (c_i > 0) on Ω_i, with H(M ∖ ⋃_iΦ_i(Ω_i)) = 0. Each Φ_i(Ω_i) is σ-compact (Ω_i is a countable union of compact sets and Φ_i is continuous), hence Borel. Put G_i := (M ∩ Φ_i(Ω_i)) ∖ ⋃_{i′<i}Φ_{i′}(Ω_{i′}). The G_i are pairwise disjoint and H-null-measurable (M is), G_i ⊆ M ∩ Φ_i(Ω_i), and M ∖ ⋃_iG_i = M ∖ ⋃_iΦ_i(Ω_i) is H-null; hence M and ⋃_iG_i are H-a.e. equal.

5. (Countable additivity.) For j ≥ j₀, F_j and F are H-integrable on M (step 3), so by countable additivity of the integral over pairwise disjoint null-measurable sets (Mathlib integral_iUnion_ae, together with M =ᵃᵉ ⋃_iG_i): ∫_M F_j dH = Σ_i a_i(j) and ∫_M F dH = Σ_i a_i, where a_i(j) := ∫_{G_i} F_j dH and a_i := ∫_{G_i} F dH. Moreover |a_i(j)|, |a_i| ≤ b_i := ∫_{G_i} G dH (step 2), and Σ_i b_i = ∫_{⋃_iG_i} G dH ≤ ∫_M G dH < ∞.

6. (One chart; parent (f).) Fix i and write Φ, Ω, K_Φ, c for Φ_i, Ω_i, K_i, c_i. Let G_K := G_i ∩ g⁻¹(K) (H-null-measurable, since g⁻¹(K) is closed), D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(G_K), u_j := g_j∘Φ and u := g∘Φ. By step 1, for j ≥ j₀, a_i(j) = ∫_{G_K} F_j dH and a_i = ∫_{G_K} F dH.
 (6a) [Jacobian bound.] For w ∈ Ω and v ∈ ℝ^k, |DΦ(w)v| ≥ c|v|: for small t ≠ 0 we have w + tv ∈ Ω and c|t||v| ≤ |Φ(w + tv) − Φ(w)| = |t·DΦ(w)v + o(t)|; divide by |t| and let t → 0. Hence the Gram matrix (⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩)_{a,b} is ≥ c²·I, so JΦ(w) ≥ c^k > 0. JΦ is continuous on Ω (Φ is C¹).
 (6b) [Change of variables.] The sibling chart_change_of_variables applies to Φ and Ω (Φ is Lipschitz and antilipschitz on the open Ω) and to A := G_K ⊆ Φ(Ω): D is L^k-null-measurable, and for every h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] that is a.e.-measurable for H⌞G_K, h∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for L^k⌞D and ∫_{G_K} h dH = ∫_D h(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dw. Two consequences: (α) if Z ⊆ ℝ^P is H-null, then h := 1_Z vanishes H⌞G_K-a.e., so ∫_D 1_Z(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dw = 0 and, by (6a), Φ(w) ∉ Z for L^k-a.e. w ∈ D; (β) applying the formula to the positive and negative parts of θ, of F_j (j ≥ j₀) and of F — all H-integrable on G_K ⊆ M ∩ g⁻¹(K) by step 3 and the hypothesis on θ — gives: θ∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for L^k⌞D and ∫_D θ(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dw = ∫_{G_K} θ dH < ∞; and for φ ∈ {F_j (j ≥ j₀), F}, w ↦ φ(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) is L^k⌞D-integrable with ∫_{G_K} φ dH = ∫_D φ(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dw.
 (6c) [Good parameters and the pointwise formula.] Fix a strongly measurable ξ̃ with ξ = ξ̃ H⌞M-a.e. For L^k-a.e. w ∈ D, with x := Φ(w) ∈ M: (i) range DΦ(w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M,θ) at x and u has Fréchet derivative L(x)∘DΦ(w) at w (sibling chart_chain_rule with U := ℝ^P and f := g; it holds for L^k-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) ⊇ D); (ii) the orientation clause holds at x and ξ(x) = ξ̃(x) (the set of points of M where this fails is H-null; use (6b)(α)). At such w: ξ(x) = ε·simpleNVector τ with ε = ±1, τ orthonormal and span τ a weighted approximate tangent space at x; since θ(x) > 0, span τ = range DΦ(w) (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Write ∂_bΦ(w) = Σ_a B_{ba}τ_a with B_{ba} := ⟨∂_bΦ(w), τ_a⟩. By the second identity of the sibling simple_nvector_algebra, simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)) = det B·simpleNVector τ; by its first identity, ‖simpleNVector τ‖² = det I = 1 and ‖simpleNVector(∂Φ(w))‖² = det(⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩) = JΦ(w)², so |det B| = JΦ(w) > 0. Let β_w be the covector v ↦ det(⟨∂_aΦ(w), v_b⟩)_{a,b}, i.e. wedgeCovectors k (fun a => ⟨∂_aΦ(w), ·⟩) (SimonGMT wedgeCovectors_apply_det); then simpleNVector(∂Φ(w))(β_w) = JΦ(w)², and s(w) := ξ̃(x)(β_w)/JΦ(w) = ε·JΦ(w)/det B ∈ {1, −1} satisfies ξ(x) = s(w)·JΦ(w)⁻¹·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)). Using A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A∘v), Dg_j(x)∂_bΦ(w) = ∂_bu_j(w) (chain rule for the C¹ maps g_j and Φ) and L(x)∂_bΦ(w) = ∂_bu(w) (by (i)), we get
 F_j(x)·JΦ(w) = s(w)·θ(x)·ω(u_j(w))(∂u_j(w)),  F(x)·JΦ(w) = s(w)·θ(x)·ω(u(w))(∂u(w)).
 (6d) [The weight.] Put ψ(w) := 1_D(w)·θ(Φ(w))·ξ̃(Φ(w))(β_w)/JΦ(w) for w ∈ Ω and ψ := 0 off Ω. It is a.e.-strongly measurable for L^k⌞Ω (D is null-measurable; θ∘Φ is a.e.-measurable on L^k⌞D by (6b)(β); ξ̃∘Φ is strongly measurable; w ↦ β_w and JΦ are continuous on Ω and JΦ > 0). By (6c), |ψ| = 1_D·(θ∘Φ) L^k-a.e., so by (6a) and (6b)(β), ∫_Ω|ψ| dw = ∫_D θ(Φ(w)) dw ≤ c^{−k}∫_D θ(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dw = c^{−k}∫_{G_K} θ dH < ∞. Thus ψ is Lebesgue integrable on Ω, and by (6b)(β) and (6c), for j ≥ j₀:
 a_i(j) = ∫_D F_j(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dw = ∫_Ω ψ(w)·ω(u_j(w))(∂u_j(w)) dw,  a_i = ∫_D F(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dw = ∫_Ω ψ(w)·ω(u(w))(∂u(w)) dw.
 (6e) [Weak continuity of minors.] u_j is (Λ′K_Φ)-Lipschitz and u is (ΛK_Φ)-Lipschitz on Ω, and sup_Ω|u_j − u| ≤ sup_{ℝ^P}|g_j − g| → 0, so u_j → u uniformly on Ω. The sibling minor_weak_continuity, applied with this Ω and ψ, α := ω (continuous with compact support), C := K_Φ·max(Λ, Λ′), u_j and u₀ := u, gives a_i(j) → a_i as j → ∞.

7. (Summation; parent (g).) By step 5, |a_i(j)| ≤ b_i for every i and every j ≥ j₀, with Σ_i b_i < ∞, and a_i(j) → a_i for every i by step 6. Dominated convergence for series (Tannery's theorem, Mathlib tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence) gives Σ_i a_i(j) → Σ_i a_i, i.e., by step 5, ∫_M F_j dH → ∫_M F dH, which is the assertion. ∎

Implementation remarks. NVector (Eucl P) k = Covector (Eucl P) k →L[ℝ] ℝ does not synthesize ContinuousENorm in this environment and the generic norm lemmas do not unify with its operator norm: avoid NVector-valued integrals, work with the real integrands F_j, F, and use the ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_* lemmas. Continuity of (A, w) ↦ A_#w is ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM composed with ContinuousLinearMap composition (as in the accepted Submission.lpf_pi_measurability). The signed change of variables in (6b)(β) is obtained from the lintegral identity of chart_change_of_variables applied to ENNReal.ofReal of the positive and negative parts.
proof_key_steps: Fixed compact target K = closed 1-neighbourhood of tsupport ω: for j ≥ j₀ both integrands vanish off g⁻¹(K); the orientation clause, ‖Dg_j‖ ≤ Λ′ and |L(x)τ_a| ≤ Λ give the dominator ‖ω‖_∞max(Λ,Λ′)^kθ1_{g⁻¹(K)}, integrable by hypothesis.
Measurability: F_j directly (continuous pulled-back covector field), F by the sibling pushforward_measurable; hence F_j (j ≥ j₀) and F are integrable on M.
Sibling c1_cover: disjoint null-measurable pieces G_i ⊆ Φ_i(Ω_i) covering M up to an H^k-null set; countable additivity splits both integrals into series dominated by Σ_i∫_{G_i}G < ∞.

On one chart: JΦ ≥ c^k; the sibling chart_change_of_variables transfers integrals and null sets to Ω; the siblings chart_chain_rule and simple_nvector_algebra give ξ(Φ(w)) = s(w)JΦ(w)⁻¹·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)), |s| = 1, so both chart integrals equal ∫_Ω ψ·ω(u)(∂u) with u = g_j∘Φ resp. g∘Φ and ψ ∈ L¹(Ω).
The sibling minor_weak_continuity gives convergence on each chart; Tannery's theorem sums the charts.
